header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, LARKANA
Criminal Misc. Application No. S-304 of 2026
[Ali Hassan and others Vs. SHO, P.S Garhi Hassan, District Jacobabad and others]
Applicants : Through Mr. Abdul Sattar Hulio,
Respondents No.1, 2 & 4 : Mr. Aitbar Ali Bullo, Deputy Prosecutor
Respondent No.3 : Through Mr. Sajid Hussain Mahessar,
body: ARBAB ALI HAKRO, J;- Through this application under section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (hereinafter referred to as “Cr.P.C.”), the applicants, who are police officials posted at Police Station Garhi Hassan, District Jacobabad, have called in question the order dated 28.08.2026 (the impugned order) passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge/Ex- Officio Justice of Peace, Thul (hereinafter referred to as “the Justice of Peace”) in Cr. Misc. Application No.620 of 2026. By that order, the application of respondent No.3 under section 22-A(6)(i) Cr.P.C. was allowed, and the SHO, P.S. Garhi Hassan, was directed to record his statement and to incorporate it in the book kept under section 154 or 155 Cr.P.C., in accordance with law.

2. The case of respondent No.3 before the Justice of Peace was that on 10.08.2026 at about 1.00 a.m., the applicants, along with other police personnel and some private persons, arrived in three police mobiles, forcibly entered his house, took away his nephew, Mashooque Ali, searched the house without a warrant, broke open the boxes and carried away silver ornaments, cash, mobile phones, a licensed rifle and other household articles, and maltreated the inmates. He stated that he went to the police station and then approached the SSP, Jacobabad, but his report was not recorded.

Criminal Misc. Application No. S-304 of 2026 Page 2 of 5 3. Learned counsel for the applicants contended that no such incident occurred; that Mashooque Ali was arrested after an encounter, in respect of which Crime No.28 of 2026 stands registered at P.S. Garhi Hassan; that respondent No.3 and his relatives are involved in a number of criminal cases, including Crime No.29 of 2026 at the same police station, and that he moved the application only to put the police under pressure; that the Justice of Peace did not consider the police report and passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner, and that, in any case, the matter ought to have been inquired into by a senior officer before any direction was given. Through a statement dated 16.11.2026, he placed on record the criminal records of respondent No.3, his brother Umed Ali, and his nephew Mashooque Ali. He relied upon Qamber Ali Shah and Khurram Khursheed.

4. Learned Deputy Prosecutor General adopted the arguments of learned counsel for the applicants and opposed the impugned order. Learned counsel for respondent No.3, on the other hand, supported the impugned order and submitted that the application disclosed cognizable offences and that the police had no authority to refuse to record the statement.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and reviewed the record.

6. The scope of section 22-A(6)(i) Cr.P.C. is now well settled. In Younas Abbas , a larger Bench of the Supreme Court held that the functions of the Justice of Peace are quasi-judicial, complementary to those of the police, and do not amount to interference in the investigation. In Qamber Ali Shah , it was explained that the Justice of Peace is not required to scrutinise the case minutely or to give any finding on the merits. He has only to see whether, from the facts narrated in the application, a cognisable offence is made out, and if so, he may direct that the statement of the complainant be recorded. The same judgment, following Muhammad Bashir, reiterates that neither the officer in charge of a police station nor anyone else has authority to hold an inquiry into the correctness of the information before recording it, and Syed Qamber Ali Shah v. Province of Sindh 2024 SCMR 1123 Khurram Khursheed v. Ex-Officio Justice of Peace 2026 MLD 1061 Younas Abbas v. Additional Sessions Judge, Chakwal PLD 2016 SC 581 Qamber Ali Shah (n.1 above)

Muhammad Bashir v. Station House Officer, Okara Cantt. PLD 2007 SC 539 Criminal Misc. Application No. S-304 of 2026 Page 3 of 5 that the check against false information is not refusal to record it but action against the informant.

7. Seen in this light, the impugned order calls for no interference on the merits. Respondent No.3 alleged house-trespass at night, removal of property and maltreatment of the inmates. Taken at face value, these allegations disclose cognizable offences. The Justice of Peace called reports from the DSP Complaint Cell and the SHO, heard the parties, and then passed a direction that is itself subject to the words “in accordance with law”. Such an order cannot be termed mechanical.

8. The pleas raised by the applicants, namely that the incident never took place, that respondent No.3 has a criminal record, and that his application is a counterblast to the cases registered against him and his relatives, are all questions of fact. They cannot be answered without evidence, and collecting evidence is the function of investigation, not of the Justice of Peace or of this Court under section 561-A Cr.P.C. The request for an inquiry before registration also cannot be accepted, as the law requires the police first to register the case and then to form an opinion on whether the facts stated are true or not.
The applicants, being police officials, stand on no different footing in this regard.

9. The record filed with the statement dated 16.11.2026 does not alter this position. Most of the cases shown in it are against the brother and the nephew of respondent No.3. Against respondent No.3 himself, only one case is shown, namely Crime No.29 of 2026. He was not named in that FIR. His name appeared in further statements of the complainant and two witnesses recorded on 14.08.2026, that is, after the date of the incident alleged by him. He has since been admitted to post-arrest bail by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Thul, vide order dated 27.08.2026. Whether his application is a reaction to that case, or his name was brought into that case because of his grievance against the police, is a matter that can only be ascertained through investigation. In any case, the pendency of a criminal case against a person does not take away his right to report a cognizable offence. Abdul Rehman Malik v. Synthia D. Ritchie 2020 SCMR 2037 Criminal Misc. Application No. S-304 of 2026 Page 4 of 5 10. The case law relied upon by learned counsel for the applicants does not assist them. In Qamber Ali Shah, this Court reversed an order that had set aside a similar direction of the Justice of Peace, based on its own assessment of the facts and by leaving the complainant to file a direct complaint, and restored the direction of the Justice of Peace. The Supreme Court held that the inherent jurisdiction cannot be used to interrupt the ordinary course of criminal procedure and that a direct complaint cannot be treated as a substitute for section 154 Cr.P.C. in every case. In Khurram Khursheed , the Lahore High Court dismissed the petition of a police official and maintained the direction of the Justice of Peace for recording the statement under section 154 Cr.P.C. against him. Both decisions thus support the impugned order.

11. The applicants are not left without protection. The registration of an FIR does not, by itself, amount to arrest. As declared in Sughran Bibi, a person named in an FIR is not to be arrested straightaway, and arrest is to be deferred until sufficient material connecting him with the offence becomes available. The Investigating Officer is bound to consider the version of the applicants as well, including the record of Crimes Nos. 28, 29 and 30 of 2026, and to report the actual facts under section 173 Cr.P.C. If the information is found false, the law provides its own course against the informant.

12. However, two aspects of the impugned order require correction. Firstly, in paragraph 4, the Justice of Peace observed that the police had acted mala fide and that the occurrence was established. He was not required to make such findings, and they cannot be allowed to influence the investigation. Secondly, the direction has been issued to the SHO of P.S. Garhi Hassan, who is himself named by respondent No.3 as an accused. It would not be fair to either side if he were to record the statement or deal with the matter.
13. For these reasons, the application is dismissed. The impugned order is maintained with the following modifications:
Khurram Khursheed (n.2 above)

Mst. Sughran Bibi v. The State PLD 2018 SC 595 Criminal Misc. Application No. S-304 of 2026 Page 5 of 5 (i) The observations made in paragraph 4 of the impugned order regarding mala fide of the police and proof of the occurrence shall be treated as tentative, confined to the decision on the application before the Justice of Peace, and shall not influence the investigation or the trial, if any.

(ii) The SSP, Jacobabad, shall ensure that the statement of respondent No.3 is recorded at P.S. Garhi Hassan by an officer other than the proposed accused, and that, if it discloses a cognisable offence, it is incorporated in the book under section 154 Cr.P.C. The investigation shall be entrusted to an officer senior in rank to the proposed accused and not posted under any of them.
(iii) No proposed accused shall be arrested unless sufficient material connecting him to the alleged offence is collected during the investigation.
(iv) If the information is found false, the police shall be at liberty to proceed against respondent No. 3 under section 182 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, in accordance with law.
14. The observations made in this order are tentative and shall not prejudice the case of either party in the investigation or in Crimes No.28, 29 and 30 of 2026.
JUDGE Zulfiqar
